newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Phnom Penh commercial flights to resume Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Phnom Penh commercial flights to resume Wednesday.

text.p: Commercial flights to and from Phnom Penh's battered airport will resume on a limited basis later on Wednesday, four days after weekend fighting in the capital closed the airport, an official said.
Keo Sophal, the secretary-general of the Civil Aviation Department, told Reuters domestic and limited international flights would resume later in the day.
"Domestic flights will start today," Keo Sophal said. "There are four domestic flights, to Siem Reap and Battambang, and two flights to Ho Chi Minh City."

He said Thailand's national flag carrier, Thai Airways International, would not be resuming its flights for the time being, apparently because of extensive damage to the airport terminal. Thai is one of the major carriers serving Cambodia.

Phnom Penh's airport was devastated over the two days of fighting and a third day of extensive looting. Practically all equipment and fixtures were stripped from the airport terminal but officials said the control tower was still functioning.
Military transport planes began arriving on Tuesday when Thailand started to evacuate its civilians trapped in the capital.
